name.help: Display name for this SMTP communication channel.

host.help: SMTP relay hostname or IP address.

port.help: SMTP port. Use 587 for STARTTLS, 465 for implicit TLS, or 25 for plain/internal relays.

encryption.help: One of starttls, ssl_tls, or none. STARTTLS is recommended for port 587.

auth_method.help: One of none, plain, login, or cram_md5.

username.help: SMTP AUTH username. Leave blank when authentication is none.

password.help: SMTP AUTH password or app password. Stored encrypted at rest.

from_name.help: Optional display name for the From header.

subject_prefix.help: Optional prefix added to every notification subject.

secretKeepHint: Leave blank to keep the stored value.
title: SMTP notification delivery
subtitle: Plugin-owned communication channel
description: This plugin owns the SMTP communication channel. It stores SMTP settings on the channel itself and does not use the removed host email-server surface.
securityDescription: Use STARTTLS for port 587, SSL/TLS for port 465, and no encryption only for trusted internal relays.
testDescription: The host test action sends a real email through this channel. Use a test recipient first if your relay pages an on-call mailbox.

step1.body: Create or choose an SMTP relay account dedicated to McHarbor notifications. Prefer an app password or scoped relay credential over a personal mailbox password.

step2.body: Set SMTP host and port. Use port 587 with encryption=starttls for most providers, port 465 with encryption=ssl_tls for implicit TLS, or port 25 with encryption=none only for trusted internal relays.

step3.body: Select the authentication method your relay supports: none, plain, login, or cram_md5. Fill Username and Password for every method except none.

step4.body: Set From address to a stable sender such as mcharbor@example.com. Some providers require this address to match the authenticated account or a verified sender identity.

step5.body: Add one or more comma-separated recipients. Start with a test mailbox, then switch to your operations or on-call distribution list once delivery is confirmed.

step6.body: Optionally set Subject prefix, for example [McHarbor Prod], so alerts are easy to filter in mail clients and ticketing systems.

step7.body: Save the channel and click Test connection. The plugin sends a real test email through the same SMTP path used for live workflow, alert, and backup events.

step8.body: If Test fails with an authentication error, verify the username, app password, sender identity, and provider SMTP AUTH settings. If STARTTLS fails, confirm the port/encryption pairing.
